text:
jess: Customer ticket #3421 — billing CSV / daily usage export shows rows attributed to the previous day. Customer says their org TZ is America/Los_Angeles and the console chart + CSV disagree. They attached a small export, see snippet below.

mike: Can you paste the minimal CSV rows and org id? I'll try to repro locally.

jess: Org ID 9876. CSV snippet: 
```
date,org_id,tokens
2026-03-15,9876,12345
2026-03-16,9876,6789
```
Customer says in Console -> Billing -> Daily the 2026-03-15 usage is showing under 2026-03-14 for them. They only see this for a handful of orgs around DST transition.

tara: quick hypothesis: our daily aggregation job truncates to UTC midnight before applying org timezone adjustment for exports. If an org is behind UTC (PST), some late-evening UTC events will be rolled back to the previous local day in the console but the CSV generation step might not shift dates consistently.

mike: I pulled the export job code. The batch job does: `date_trunc('day', event_ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') as day_utc` then groups by day_utc. The CSV formatter later does `format_day(day_utc, org_tz)` — but there's a codepath in exports v2 that calls `format_day` with `timezone=None` if the org has a legacy flag. Looks like a boolean flip introduced in 2026-01 release.

sam: Which release/PR? We need to know if billing calculations were affected or just CSV labels. If it's only CSV labeling we can fast-follow with a patch; if aggregation used UTC for sums we might have subtotal mismatches.

mike: PR #1428 (2026-01-08) added a fallback for org timezone to avoid failing exports for orgs without tz set. The logic mistakenly used `if org.tz is None or org.tz == '' then use None` which the formatter treats as UTC. So: aggregate by UTC day, format by UTC day — results are shifted for orgs in negative offsets.

tara: Repro steps I used locally:
1) Set org.tz = "America/Los_Angeles" on org 9876
2) Inject events with timestamps `2026-03-15T07:30:00Z` (which is 00:30 PDT on 3/15)
3) Run nightly agg: `SELECT date_trunc('day', event_ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') as day_utc, sum(tokens) FROM events WHERE org_id=9876 GROUP BY day_utc;` -> returns 2026-03-15
4) Run CSV export path v2 which incorrectly does `format_day(day_utc)` -> 2026-03-15 (UTC) but console display layer applies `day_utc AT TIME ZONE 'America/Los_Angeles'` -> shows as 2026-03-14 in some UI paths.

mike: TL;DR we have two inconsistent places: aggregation/formatting path (exports service) and console rendering path. The root cause is the fallback-to-None in exports v2 that ends up interpreting day buckets in UTC for display.

jess: Customer wants to know: is billing total wrong or just the daily label?

sam: I looked at subtotal math; sums are correct (tokens totals match across endpoints) — it's only the bucket label/date shift. So billing amounts shouldn't be affected but daily line-items appear on previous day for some orgs.

mike: Proposed fix: change exports v2 to always pass explicit org tz when known; fallback to account settings; avoid None. Quick patch: in exports service, replace `tz = org.tz or None` with `tz = org.tz if org.tz else 'UTC'` and ensure formatter takes tz param. I'll open a PR and mark as hotfix.

tara: Also add unit test covering DST edge cases and a small e2e test that compares console chart date buckets vs CSV date labels for sample org.

mike: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/exports/pull/1709 — includes patch + test + release notes. Deploy plan: canary to staging, smoke on 10 orgs, then prod rollout over 30m.

export-bot: deploy queued: exports:v2.1.5-hotfix -> staging (canary 3/10 pods)

jess: I'll reply to the customer: thanks for flagging — explains that totals are intact and this is a CSV/label mismatch tied to timezone handling; we're rolling a hotfix and will re-generate your export once deployed. ETA ~1-2 hours for staging verification, 2-4 hours for prod.

mike: After prod deploy, we should re-run their export and attach corrected CSV and also re-index console daily cache for org 9876 for the affected date range (2026-03-13..2026-03-17). I can run reindex script: `scripts/reindex_daily_buckets --org 9876 --from 2026-03-13 --to 2026-03-17`

jess: Great. I'll mark ticket #3421 P1 and send customer short note. :thumbsup:

sam: Follow-up: add a monitoring alert for export-v2 where `tz_param` is null in logs for >0.1% of exports in a day. That will catch regressions.

tara: I'll add the DST unit tests to the nightly pipeline as well.

jess: leaving thread open until deploy verifies, will post results here.
